browser_regressions.finding: Saving after recovery did not switch back to the ontology tab, so the new version could not be located.
browser_regressions.fix: Set ontology tab and locate the accepted version after a guarded library refresh.

browser_regressions.finding: The change event on input blur rebuilt recovery buttons between pointer events and lost the inspection click.
browser_regressions.fix: Persist input without rebuilding recovery controls unless the storage warning changes; a focused unit regression and final browser flow pass.

checks.syntax: Changed Python modules AST-parse; node --check passed for ontology_save.js and learning.js.
checks.visual_review: Inspected light/dark 1440px screenshots showing original save v2, later version v3, retained local text and explicit recovery actions. Eight desktop layouts pass overflow and button hit-testing.

behavior.atomic_save: Ontology version, search index, audit and existing asset_save_requests row commit together; receipt failure rolls back all writes.
behavior.idempotency: Optional request_id binds operation ontology.revise, base_ref and full content. Exact replay returns the accepted version even after subsequent revisions or lifecycle/source changes.
behavior.inspection: GET ontology-saves/request_id?base_ref=ref reads the original receipt and latest version in one authorized snapshot. A newer version alone never proves the original save succeeded.
behavior.editing: Local ontology content and immutable save attempts are retained separately in sessionStorage scoped by tenant, principal, workspace and asset.
behavior.recovery: Explicit original retry or explicit adoption/rebase; confirmation protects later edits before viewing saved results or adopting latest content.
behavior.ownership: Session, route and scope guards fence late reads and POST replies. Normal close preserves edits; storage failure keeps the editor open.
behavior.compatibility: Existing asset save receipt schema is reused; request_hash is an additive response field. Unkeyed legacy ontology revisions retain version conflict behavior.

limitations: Tab sessionStorage recovery depends on browser session behavior; accepted versions and receipts remain server records.
Explicitly keeping local content against a newer version does not automatically merge the other revision.
Closing a pending view or discarding its local recovery copy does not cancel an in-flight server save.
Only submissions with request_id have exact receipt-based retries; legacy calls without it remain supported.
No external model was invoked; tests use temporary data and offline generation.
No release package was built or deployed.
